cohort: The study included 10,969 pregnant women who had an outpatient visit with Obstetrics and Gynecology and a delivery encounter from January 1, 2020, through June 30, 2022, within a large health system.
finding: Black race was associated with a lower likelihood of having a penicillin allergy label, while older age (32-51 years) and atopic conditions (rhinitis, asthma, or eczema) were associated with a higher likelihood of having a penicillin allergy label during pregnancy.
